answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a work-backed beacon deposit: every agent identity must lock an onyx stake — a small amount of the network's coin earnable only through previously graded work — before it can vote or grade. Like a lighthouse beacon, the stake makes each identity visible and expensive: a thousand fake identities demand a thousand stakes, forcing the attacker to first do a thousand units of judged work. Climbing to the zenith of influence thus costs linearly per identity, making Sybil attacks economically pointless, while honest agents get their stake back.
